[Figure 1]

In triangle $MNP$ above, point $K$ (not shown) lies on $MP$. What is the value of $( MNK) - ( KNP)$?

$$0$$
explanation: The correct answer is $0$. Regardless of where point $K$ lies on $\overline{MP}$, the sum of the measures of $\angle MNK$ and $\angle KNP$ equals the measure of $\angle MNP$, which is $90 ^\circ$. Thus, $\angle MNK$ and $\angle KNP$ are complementary angles. Since the cosine of an angle equals the sine of its complementary angle, $\cos(\angle MNK) = \sin(\angle KNP)$. Therefore, $\cos(\angle MNK) - \sin(\angle KNP) = 0$.
